description: Any window from your Mac, live on your iPhone or iPad. Touch, Apple Pencil, trackpad and keys. Free, open source, no servers.

latest_release.name: Sill 0.6.0
latest_release.body:
Sill 0.6.0 brings the clipboard both ways between your Mac and your iPhone or iPad, sound from your Mac as a beta, and a locked Mac that shows only its lock screen. On the device there's more: a hardware keyboard and trackpad that work as soon as the picture shows, pinch to zoom, Larger Picture on iPhone, typing in Chinese, Japanese and Korean, your Mac computers as tiles, and the tour once more with what's new marked. On the Mac, Virtual Display and Send Audio are on by default, a window Sill resized goes back to its own frame, and security fixes from a scan of the code.

**One version for both apps.** This is Sill for Mac 0.6.0 (1276), and it goes with Sill for iPhone and iPad 0.6.0 (1276), built from the same commit. Each half still works with the other's 0.5.1, without the clipboard, the sound and the locked Mac's cover: those need both apps at 0.6.0. Sill for iPhone and iPad 0.6.0 is on the App Store: (https://apps.apple.com/app/id6816359860). If you build it from source, build it from this release's tag.

**New for the iPhone and iPad**
- **Larger Picture**, in Settings on iPhone: held upright, a window's picture takes the place of the window thumbnails and reaches down to where the keyboard comes up. Set a window's text size with Aa and your Mac makes it as tall as the picture. The Desktop keeps the usual layout.
- **A hardware keyboard and trackpad**: with a keyboard attached, what you type goes to your Mac as soon as its picture shows, Esc included, without the Keyboard button. Two fingers on a trackpad, or a mouse's scroll wheel, now scroll the window under the pointer.
- **Reverse Scrolling**, in Settings: a finger dragged over the picture, or two fingers on the trackpad below it, scroll the other way. A trackpad or mouse connected to your iPad keeps following its Natural Scrolling setting.
- **Pinch to zoom**: two fingers zoom the picture up to 5× around the point between them, and move it while it's zoomed. Taps, clicks and scrolls land on what you see under your finger. Pinch all the way out to see everything again.
- **Window controls sooner**: hold a window's thumbnail and its close, minimize and full-screen controls show after half a second, not a second and a half. Hold to Show Window Controls, in Settings, sets it from 0.2 to 2 seconds.
- **Type in Chinese, Japanese, Korean** and other languages that compose their text, and dictate: you compose and choose on your iPhone or iPad, with the keyboards and dictation languages you set up in Settings, and what you choose is typed on your Mac.
- **Your Mac computers as tiles**, each with its screen as you last left it. Touch and hold one to put it in a group, such as Home or Work. To list them instead, tap the button beside Connect to a Mac; Sill remembers your choice.
- **Copy and paste** between your Mac and your iPhone or iPad: text you copy on your Mac is ready to paste here, and Paste in Sill pastes what you copied here where your Mac's cursor is. Share Clipboard, in Sill's settings on either, turns it off and on. It needs Sill for Mac 0.6.0.
- **Sound from your Mac**, a beta feature: your iPhone or iPad plays the sound of the window you're using, or of every app for the Desktop, a moment behind the picture. Send Audio, in Sill's settings on your iPhone or iPad or in the Sill menu on your Mac, turns it off and on for every device, and Mute in Sill's settings silences it on one device. It needs Sill for Mac 0.6.0.
- **Aa starts at Off**, which leaves your Mac's window as it is, and sliding it back to Off puts a window Sill resized back to its own size right away (with Sill for Mac 0.6.0; with an earlier one, Off only stops the resizing). On Sill's virtual display a window always fits, so Aa has no Off there. Aa is dimmed while the Desktop shows: it sizes a window.

detail.readme_excerpt:
# Sill

Any window from your Mac, on your iPhone and iPad.

Sill shows a window from your Mac, or the whole desktop, on your iPhone or
iPad. You use it there with touch, a trackpad, a keyboard or Apple Pencil.
Sill for Mac captures the window, encodes it as HEVC video and sends it to the
Sill app on your device. Your taps, clicks, scrolls and keys go back to your
Mac. Your Mac and your device connect on the same network, over a USB cable,
with Direct Wireless Connection when they share no network, or through your
own VPN, such as Tailscale, with Remote Access. There is no account and no
server in between.

**[getsill.app](https://getsill.app)** ·
[Download for Mac](https://getsill.app/download) ·
[Support](https://getsill.app/support) ·
[Privacy](https://getsill.app/privacy) ·
[Terms](https://getsill.app/terms)

[![CI](https://github.com/Saffsanity/sill/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg?branch=main)](https://github.com/Saffsanity/sill/actions/workflows/ci.yml)

[![Download on the App Store](https://tools.applemediaservices.com/api/badges/download-on-the-app-store/black/en-us?size=250x83)](https://apps.apple.com/app/id6816359860)

Sill for Mac is a free, notarized download from
[getsill.app](https://getsill.app/download); with [Homebrew](https://brew.sh),
`brew install --cask saffsanity/sill/sill` installs the same download from
Sill's own [tap](https://github.com/Saffsanity/homebrew-sill). Sill for iPhone
and iPad is free on the [App Store](https://apps.apple.com/app/id6816359860),
and you can also build it from source (below).

To try the next version before it ships: Sill for iPhone and iPad has a
[public beta on TestFlight](https://testflight.apple.com/join/6v7nqyn3), and Sill for Mac
has [nightly builds](https://github.com/Saffsanity/sill/releases/tag/nightly) on
GitHub, notarized like a release but not supported. Your devices stay paired
(a nightly uses the release's identity), and Sill's update check never offers
a nightly: the release above is the one to use.

Sill has layouts of its own.
